incident.summary: The prior Financial binding repair incorrectly required a UAOS article task ID and Financial article state ID to be equal, and cached child implementation/version/CI details in the parent router state.

root_cause: UAOS modeled parent continuity as shared child identity rather than delegation plus an opaque domain-owned reference. This caused the parent router to know Financial implementation details that belong only to the child business authority.
preserved_repairs: Financial business workflow remains external and unique; the retired parent domains/financial_writing package stays removed.
BINDING_POLICY continues to delegate mutation hierarchy to AUTHORITY_WRITE_POLICY instead of duplicating it.

changes: Make BINDING_POLICY state the generic default that parent controller identity and domain business identity are distinct namespaces.
Reduce financial-writing:main to a UAOS domain router with optional opaque child state reference only.
Remove child package/profile/validator/release/CI implementation details from parent router state.
Update task discovery metadata to describe delegation to the independent Financial owner.
Add regression tests preventing task-ID equality and child implementation-detail caching from returning.

acceptance: Financial router contains no same-ID rule or child internal validator symbol
Financial router contains no child package/profile/release/CI pins
parent stores only registration metadata and optional opaque child reference
generic binding policy preserves distinct identity namespaces by default
